title: Three Ways Plates Meet
objective: After this level you can name divergent, convergent and transform plate boundaries and give a real example of each.
summary: Divergent boundaries make crust, transform boundaries neither make nor destroy it, and convergent ones come in three kinds: ocean-continent, ocean-ocean, continent-continent.

cards.headline: In Iceland, two plates are pulling a valley open.
cards.body: At Þingvellir, the North American and Eurasian plates break apart, and the land between them sinks into a rift, spreading about 2 cm a year. That's one way plates meet. There are two others, and one of them comes in three kinds.

cards.headline: Pulling apart, sliding past
cards.body: You met the three boundary types in World Geography. Here's the next layer: what each does to the crust. At a divergent boundary, plates move apart and magma pushing up from the mantle makes new crust. At a transform boundary, plates slide sideways past each other, and crust is neither made nor destroyed. California's San Andreas Fault is one; Level 16 takes you there.

items.label: Ocean meets continent
points: The ocean plate dives under the continent
Feeds volcanoes, as in the Andes and Cascades
Example: the Nazca Plate under South America built the Andes

items.label: Ocean meets ocean
points: One ocean plate dives under the other
A deep trench and a curved chain of volcanic islands
Example: the Mariana Trench and Islands

items.label: Continent meets continent
points: Neither dives easily, so the crust crumples upward
Example: India hit Asia about 50 million years ago and built the Himalayas

mascot.line: This table connects to everything ahead: the kind of boundary sets the faults, the quakes and the volcanoes you get.

cards.headline: Plate boundaries: sorted
learned: Divergent: new crust from rising magma
Transform: crust neither made nor destroyed

questions.prompt: At which kind of plate boundary is crust neither made nor destroyed?

options.label: Convergent
options.rationale: Crust dives down and is destroyed there.

options.label: A rift valley
options.rationale: A rift is where plates pull apart and crust forms.

questions.explanation: At transform boundaries, plates slide past each other sideways, so crust is neither produced nor destroyed.

questions.prompt: Match each kind of plate collision with an example.
questions.explanation: The Nazca Plate diving under South America built the Andes, ocean meeting ocean made the Mariana Trench, and India hitting Asia built the Himalayas.

questions.prompt: Iceland's rift and the Andes sit on different kinds of plate boundary. What is the difference?

options.label: Both are places where plates collide head-on
Both are transform boundaries sliding past
Iceland's plates collide head-on; at the Andes, the plates pull apart
Iceland's plates pull apart; at the Andes, one dives under another

questions.explanation: Iceland sits on a divergent boundary; the Andes rise where the Nazca Plate dives under South America.
